documents.source_category: Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026

financials_interim.notes: Mercantile Investments and Finance PLC (MERC) is a licensed finance company (NBFI); this filing presents a SINGLE set of financial statements for 'the Company' only -- Investment in associates (Rs.1,999,822k) is equity-accounted, not consolidated, and no subsidiaries exist -- so basis=GROUP is entered by this project's convention for single-entity filings (same figures would apply to a COMPANY row, so no duplicate row entered). MERC's fiscal year runs April-March (confirmed by SOFP comparative '31 March 2026'), so 'For 03 months ended 30 June 2026' is genuinely Q1 FY2026/27 with no quarter-vs-cumulative ambiguity. Per NBFI convention: revenue = 'Total operating income' (2,742,337, the filing's own top-line subtotal = net interest income + net fee income + other operating income); operating_profit = 'Operating profit before tax on financial services' (979,926), the company's own subtotal; profit_before_tax = 'Profit before taxation from operations' (713,557), which already includes 'Share of associate company's profit, net of tax' (54,936); tax_expense = 'Income tax expenses' (319,130) -- note this excludes the separate 'Tax on financial services' line (321,305), which is netted off BEFORE profit_before_tax (i.e. embedded in the path from operating_profit to profit_before_tax) rather than after, unlike MBSL/PMB/LOFC where VAT/SSCL-on-financial-services sits alongside income tax below PBT -- flagged as a genuine structural difference in this filing's presentation, not an extraction error. profit_after_tax = 'Profit for the period' (394,427). Revenue (Total operating income) grew 65.2% YoY (2,742,337 vs 1,659,772) -- per the Segments Information note (p.5), this is overwhelmingly driven by the LOANS & ADVANCES segment, whose external operating income rose from Rs.1,513,778k to Rs.3,524,544k (+132.9%, a Rs.2,010,766k absolute increase that alone accounts for ~84% of the Rs.2,393,767k total income increase across all segments); the Finance Lease segment grew a comparatively modest 23.6% (Rs.1,492,844k to Rs.1,845,452k) and Investments grew 13.5% (Rs.166,867k to Rs.189,408k). Impairment charges rose even faster (Rs.64,466k to Rs.282,110k, +337.6%) reflecting the much larger loan book, but PBT still grew 125.2% and PAT grew 95.0% (394,427 vs 202,233) as revenue growth outpaced both impairment and operating-expense growth. Inventories (Rs.355,875k) IS explicitly disclosed as a distinct SOFP line in this filing (unlike CDB/LOFC/MBSL where no such line exists) -- populated here as a deliberate deviation from the usual 'leave inventory blank' NBFI convention, because the company itself presents it as a discrete balance-sheet item (likely repossessed lease/HP stock). trade_receivables/trade_payables left blank -- not disclosed as such; 'Other financial assets'/'Other non financial assets' and 'Other liabilities' are not itemised as trade in nature. current_assets/current_liabilities left blank -- liquidity-ordered SOFP, no current/non-current split. short_term_borrowings = 'Bank overdrafts' (1,352,677); long_term_borrowings = 'Financial liabilities at amortised cost - Debt instruments issued and other borrowings' (43,719,027). 'Deposits due to customers' (64,605,815) and 'Lease liability' (673,885) are deliberately EXCLUDED from borrowings -- deposits are funding not debt, and the lease liability is treated as non-debt per this project's convention for small lease liabilities. shares_in_issue = 634,600,000 (actual ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026, per note 4) -- NOTE this differs from the 616,190,000 WEIGHTED-AVERAGE shares used by the company itself to compute both EPS and Net Assets per Share, because the Rights Issue (33,400,000 new shares, raising Rs.1,102.2m) completed and listed only on 4 June 2026, partway through the quarter; cross-check ties to the weighted-average basis: EPS 0.64 = 394,427k/616,190k = 0.6402 (ties), and NAV/share 28.20 = 17,376,721k/616,196k = 28.20 (ties) -- NOT to period-end shares (17,376,721k/634,600k would give 27.38, which does NOT match the disclosed Rs.28.20 NAV/share). This is flagged explicitly since it is exactly the 'shares_in_issue vs disclosed EPS' cross-check the project instructions call for, and the mismatch here has a clear, filing-disclosed cause (note 6, mid-period Rights Issue) rather than being an extraction error. Cash flow statement (p.4) is genuinely quarter-only ('For 03 months ended 30 June'), no cumulative-vs-quarter ambiguity. capex = Purchase of PPE (80,470) + Acquisition of intangible assets (1,934) = 82,404, ties exactly to the segment note's own 'Capital expenditure' figure of 82,404 (p.5).

interim_updates.note_text: Mercantile Investments and Finance PLC (MERC) reported strong YoY growth for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026): Total operating income rose 65.2% to Rs.2,742.34mn from Rs.1,659.77mn, Profit before taxation from operations rose 125.2% to Rs.713.56mn from Rs.316.85mn, and Profit for the period rose 95.0% to Rs.394.43mn from Rs.202.23mn; EPS rose to Rs.0.64 from Rs.0.34. Per the Segments Information note (p.5), growth is overwhelmingly driven by the LOANS & ADVANCES segment, whose external operating income rose from Rs.1,513.78mn to Rs.3,524.54mn (+132.9%, a Rs.2,010.77mn absolute increase that alone accounts for approximately 84% of the Rs.2,393.77mn total operating-income increase across all segments). The Finance Lease segment grew a comparatively modest 23.6% (Rs.1,492.84mn to Rs.1,845.45mn) and the Investments segment grew 13.5% (Rs.166.87mn to Rs.189.41mn). Impairment charges for loans and receivables rose even faster than revenue, +337.6% to Rs.282.11mn from Rs.64.47mn -- reflecting the much larger loan book -- but Profit before tax still grew 125.2% and Profit for the period grew 95.0% as revenue growth outpaced both the impairment increase and operating-expense growth (Personnel expenses +22.1% to Rs.713.36mn; Depreciation/amortisation +27.2% to Rs.97.48mn; Other operating expenses +37.7% to Rs.669.47mn). Tax on financial services (embedded before Profit before taxation, distinct from Income tax expenses) rose 97.3% to Rs.321.31mn from Rs.162.87mn; Income tax expenses (the schema's tax_expense field) rose 178.4% to Rs.319.13mn from Rs.114.61mn -- income tax growing faster than pretax profit is why PAT growth (95.0%) trailed PBT growth (125.2%). Operating margin improved to 35.7% from 27.0%, and net margin improved to 14.4% from 12.2%. A mid-period Rights Issue (33,400,000 new shares, raising Rs.1,102.2mn, listed 4 June 2026) increased shares in issue to 634,600,000 at period-end from a lower weighted-average base of 616,190,000 used for the EPS calculation -- this dilutes the period-end share count relative to the profit-generating base but does not distort the reported EPS figure, which is correctly computed on the weighted-average basis.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is MERC's first financial_statements/interim_updates entry in this DB (no closer prior quarter has been collected). Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) the filing does not disclose impairment charges broken out by segment (Loans & Advances vs Finance Lease vs Investments), so the 337.6% YoY rise in impairment cannot be attributed to a specific segment from this document alone, even though the Loans & Advances segment is clearly the volume driver; (2) no qualitative commentary (MD&A/directors' review) is included explaining the mechanism behind the Loans & Advances segment's 132.9% income growth (e.g. new product launch, rate repricing, or pure volume growth) beyond the segmental figures themselves; (3) the mid-period Rights Issue (33,400,000 shares, Rs.1,102.2mn, listed 4 June 2026, per Note 6) is disclosed as to size and timing but the filing does not state the intended use of proceeds.
interim_updates.takeaway: MERC's strong Q1 FY2026/27 growth (revenue +65.2%, PAT +95.0%) is driven overwhelmingly by the Loans & Advances segment, whose external operating income more than doubled (+132.9% YoY, Rs.2,010.77mn absolute increase) and alone accounts for roughly 84% of total income growth -- Finance Lease and Investments grew far more modestly. The main cost to monitor is credit quality: impairment charges for loans and receivables nearly quadrupled (+337.6% to Rs.282.11mn) as the loan book scaled, and while revenue growth comfortably outpaced this increase this quarter, the pace of impairment growth (338%) well exceeding the pace of income growth (65%) is worth tracking if it continues. A mid-period Rights Issue (Rs.1,102.2mn, listed 4 June 2026) has already lifted the period-end share count to 634,600,000, which will raise the bar for per-share growth in subsequent quarters even though it did not distort this quarter's correctly weighted-average-based EPS of Rs.0.64.

operational_highlights: Total operating income Rs.2,742.34mn, +65.2% YoY (Q1 FY2025/26: Rs.1,659.77mn); Profit before taxation from operations Rs.713.56mn, +125.2% YoY; Profit for the period Rs.394.43mn, +95.0% YoY; EPS Rs.0.64 (Q1 FY2025/26: Rs.0.34).

Loans & Advances segment external operating income +132.9% YoY to Rs.3,524.54mn (from Rs.1,513.78mn) -- a Rs.2,010.77mn increase accounting for ~84% of the total Rs.2,393.77mn operating-income growth.
Finance Lease segment income +23.6% YoY to Rs.1,845.45mn; Investments segment +13.5% YoY to Rs.189.41mn -- both grew far more modestly than Loans & Advances.
Impairment charges for loans and receivables +337.6% YoY to Rs.282.11mn (from Rs.64.47mn), reflecting the larger loan book; still outpaced by revenue growth so profit still rose.
Mid-period Rights Issue of 33,400,000 shares (Rs.1,102.2mn, listed 4 June 2026) raised period-end shares in issue to 634,600,000 vs a weighted-average EPS base of 616,190,000.
Operating margin improved to 35.7% from 27.0%; net margin improved to 14.4% from 12.2%.
key_drivers: Loans & Advances segment external operating income growth of 132.9% YoY (Rs.2,010.77mn absolute increase, ~84% of total income growth) is the dominant driver of the 65.2% rise in Total operating income and the resulting profit growth.
Impairment charges for loans and receivables rose 337.6% YoY to Rs.282.11mn, a meaningful offsetting cost tied directly to the larger loan book, though not large enough to prevent PBT/PAT growth.
Income tax expenses grew faster (+178.4% to Rs.319.13mn) than Profit before taxation (+125.2%), which is why PAT growth (95.0%) trailed PBT growth despite the strong underlying operating performance.
